newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey welcomes EU Cyprus accession plan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey welcomes EU Cyprus accession plan.

text.p: Turkey said on Wednesday it welcomed a European Union plan to involve Turkish Cypriots in the process of admitting the divided island to the bloc.

"The latest attitude of the EU members, except Greece, was a positive step towards understanding that Cyprus does not consist only of the Greek Cypriot part," Omer Akbel, spokesman at the foreign ministry, told reporters.
Greece on Tuesday threatened to delay the European Union enlargement after the rest of the EU proposed on Monday to involve the Turkish Cypriot community in talks on the entry of Cyprus.

Dutch European Affairs Minister Michiel Patijn said Cypriot accession to the 15-nation bloc would be politically and almost physically impossible without at least some progress between the island's divided Greek and Turkish communities.
Akbel said the EU plans appeared to go some way towards supporting Turkey's thesis that the Greek Cypriot-led government did not have the authority to represent the whole island.
The international community recognises the Greek Cypriot-led government in the south as the island's only government. It is due to start accession negotiations with the bloc next year.
Turkish Cypriots living in the north have set up a breakaway state whose independence is recognised only by Turkey, which keeps some 30,000 troops there.

United Nations-led attempts to reunite the island under a federal umbrella have made little progress while tension between Greek and Turkish Cypriots has risen after killings at the ceasefire line and a decision by Greek Cypriots to buy anti-aircraft missiles from Russia.
That deal prompted threats from Turkey of a military strike to block deployment of the missiles, due in 16 months.
Turkey invaded the northern third of Cyprus in 1974, in response to Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia that was backed by Athens.
